title: PROFINET: TimeAware Dissection and RSI FREQ block fix
description:
TimeAware bit dissected for ARProperties
and cyclic frames updated accordingly.
Also small length problem fixed in RSI FREQ block dissection.

notes.body:
added 71 commits
  • 64f27977...e4a33d22 - 70 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • f810ad27 - PROFINET: TimeAware Dissection and RSI FREQ block fix
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6000/diffs?diff_id=316860302&start_sha=64f279774a1a104cc1b224ac55eb0b5948c25a4b)

global variable is never a good idea for wireshark on dissection
why don't use proto_get/set_data ?
I didn't use proto_get/set_data before and I couldn't find these functions in the code. Could you please give me an example usage of these functions ? I will fix this accordingly.
oups, it is p_add_proto_data/p_get_proto_data/p_set_proto_data (from epan/proto_data.h)

I tried to use these functions but problem is When I p_add_proto_data from packet-dcerpc-pn-io.c, I couldn't p_get_proto_data from packet-pn-rt.c. Basically as far as I understood, usage of these functions must be in same folder. But I have to access is_time_aware info from another folder.
My goal here is, if time_aware ARBlock comes, then all cyclic frames must be set as RT-Stream according to their frameID. Otherwise they must be RTC3. This is according to PROFINET MU2 standart.

@alagoutte If this is not acceptible anyway, I can remove that part of implementation. At least we can merge the rest. But we will need that part at some point. Maybe I can open an issue after merging the rest. Because I'm a Siemens developer and we need to dissect RT-Stream Cyclic frames at some point. ( I already created a merge request for our TSN implementation )
You need to add a line `#include <epan/proto_data.h>` in the top of `packet-pn-rt.c` the way it is already present in `packet-dcerpc-pn-io.c` in order to use the functions.

@johnthacker I added that. I managed to compile and try with these functions. Could you please check the png I added ? I tried to explain my problem. ![TimeAware](/uploads/1dd9c7c4cfe07b9b06fcb06e16b4b2eb/TimeAware.PNG)

Ah, I see. Yes, `p_[add|get]_proto_data` is for data for a protocol for a particular frame. (Either packet-scoped to share data between dissectors / functions in a dissector, or file-scoped to save information associated with a packet for multiple passes.)

If you need to access information from a previous packet, some global data that is true for a particular conversation, then what you want is `conversation_[get|set]_proto_data`. It looks like that dissector already uses conversations, so using those functions shouldn't be too hard.

Note that if you just use a global and access it from a later packet, things could be wrong if the capture file contains multiple conversations interleaved.

Hello John, I tried conversation approach but problem is First Frame and Cyclic Frames mentioned above are not in same conversation too. So I can not bind them via conversations too. Just an example from my pcap: 
![Cyclic](/uploads/1dc95fbb92ba11c4854d960f6208f2dc/Cyclic.PNG)

How does the protocol know that particular First Frames and Cyclic Frames are associated with each other, in a way that it wouldn't cause a problem if transactions are interleaved? You need to use that to associate them somehow (which can mean defining a new conversation endpoint type, or can mean managing it with an internal data structure.)

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6000/diffs?diff_id=341809370&start_sha=343683bccc9d0f0d3706d0ca3bcda13f76e7a36e#1b36b7bfc776219d717795216f2f236f9cff3255_868_869)
Hi John, I finally found a way to dissect this frames without global variables. Could you please check if it is okay or not ? Thanks for your help
@johnthacker Hello John, Should I create a new Merge Request for this ? Or Is this one okay ? Kind Regards
